title: Truthfulness
note: வாய்மை is the nature of truth. It forbids lying, which mostly springs from desire and wealth, so it follows the chapters on false conduct and on not stealing.

couplets.plain: What is truthfulness? It is speech with no harm in it at all.
couplets.pm: If you ask what deserves the name of truth, it is saying words that do not cause the least harm to any other being. So reporting what happened isn’t enough. A fact that does no harm is truth, and a fact that does harm is a lie.

links.quote: speech with no harm in it at all
no harm in it at all

couplets.plain: Even a lie counts as truthfulness, if it brings good with no fault in it.
couplets.pm: If false words bring others good free of fault, they too count as truthful. That good is righteousness: a life facing ruin or death is saved by the lie and is glad. True speech is a fact that does no harm, or an untruth that does good. A lie is an untruth that does no good, or a fact that does harm.

links.quote: Even a lie counts as truthfulness
links.reason: Stretches truthfulness to cover even a lie, so long as the good it brings has no fault in it.

links.quote: if it brings good with no fault in it
links.reason: Sets the bar for a lie very high: the good it brings must be free of all fault.

couplets.plain: Don’t lie about what your own heart knows. Once you have lied, your own heart will burn you.
couplets.pm: Don’t lie about something your heart knows, thinking that others don’t know it. If you lie, the heart that knows stands witness to the sin and brings on you the suffering that is its fruit. A lie can’t stay hidden, so it mustn’t be told.

links.quote: your own heart will burn you
links.reason: Makes the liar their own punisher, burned from within once the lie is told.

links.quote: Don’t lie about what your own heart knows
links.reason: Warns anyone about to lie that their own heart will burn them for it afterwards.

couplets.plain: Live without lying in your heart, and you will live in the hearts of all the world.
couplets.pm: If you live true to your heart, not lying but speaking the truth, you live in the hearts of all the great. Seeing how hard this righteousness is, the great will think of you always. This is its reward in this life.

links.quote: you will live in the hearts of all the world
links.reason: Promises anyone who lives without lying a place in every heart.

couplets.plain: If you speak truth from the heart, you stand above those who practise penance and give alms as well.
couplets.pm: If you speak the truth so that it sits with your heart, you are greater than those who do penance and give alms together. What is done within, with mind and speech, yields more than what is done outwardly with the body.

links.quote: you stand above those who practise penance and give alms

couplets.plain: There is no renown like never lying. Without any toil, it gives you all righteousness.
couplets.pm: In this life, nothing brings renown as not lying does. For the next life, it gives you all righteousness with no strain on the body. Household life takes the toil of gathering wealth, and renunciation the toil of fasting. Not lying gives the fruit of both without either.

links.quote: Without any toil, it gives you all righteousness
links.reason: Its reward needs no toil: not lying is enough to bring all righteousness.

couplets.plain: If you can keep to not lying, not lying, then it is good to leave other righteous deeds undone, quite undone.
couplets.pm: If you can do this one thing, not lying and not lying, it is good not to do other righteous deeds, not to do them. Taking on many, you are sure to slip in some and fall into fault, so keep to this one without fail. It gives the fruit of them all. He rejects the reading that other righteous deeds are good only if you don’t lie.

links.reason: Treats a life with no lie in it as enough, leaving other righteous deeds nothing to add.

couplets.plain: Water gives you outer purity. Inner purity is seen through truthfulness.
couplets.pm: Water alone makes the body clean, and in the same way truthfulness makes the mind pure. A clean body is one free of ritual impurity, and a pure mind is one that knows the truth. So those who renounce need both kinds of purity.

links.quote: Inner purity is seen through truthfulness
links.reason: Gives the test of an inner purity that water can’t reach: is this person truthful?
Sets truthfulness to do for the inside what water does for the outside.

couplets.plain: Not every lamp is a lamp. To the worthy, the only lamp is the lamp of not lying.
couplets.pm: The world’s lamps, the sun, the moon and fire, drive out outer darkness and are no lamps at all. For those made complete by renunciation, the lamp is not lying, which drives out the darkness of the mind, ignorance. Some take this to mean the brightness that comes from learning and the like, and he doesn’t follow them.

links.quote: To the worthy, the only lamp is the lamp of not lying
links.reason: Among all lamps, the worthy give the name of lamp to not lying and nothing else.
Sets not lying beside every other lamp and finds it the only true one.

couplets.plain: Of all we have seen to be true, nothing at all is better than truthfulness.
couplets.pm: In all the books we have seen to be true, no other righteousness is ranked above truthfulness in any way. Those books are the scriptures spoken in compassion by the divine ones, who are free of confusion, desire and anger, for the good of the world. They all agree on this.

links.quote: nothing at all is better than truthfulness
links.reason: Of all the poet has seen to be true, nothing stands higher than truthfulness.

ideaLinks.quote: There is no renown like never lying
ideaLinks.reason: The highest renown anyone can win comes from never lying.
